title: Pool Cadence Orchestrator — Mini UX Prototype for Dedicated Capacity Controls
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design and validate a compact, operator-focused widget (the 'Cadence Orchestrator') for Redwood Console that lets platform operators schedule and preview dedicated GPU pool capacity cadence: autoscale policies, time-bounded burst slots, cost/latency impact preview, and quick rollback. The mini UX targets high-signal controls for on-call and SREs who need to act quickly during traffic patterns or cost events without navigating the full reserve console.
acceptance_criteria: Mid-fidelity prototype demonstrates: a) schedule editor for slot-based bursts, b) autoscale hysteresis slider, c) cost delta preview for each change, d) one-click rollback to previous cadence
Prototype validated in usability sessions with >=6 operators and feedback documented
Design handoff package includes React-ready tokens, interaction specs, and API contract notes for ENG-12884
Edge-case flows documented: overlapping burst windows, emergency immediate-burst, and policy fallbacks to model variants
Design signed off by PM (Rina Patel) and Eng lead (Diego Alvarez)
comments: 2026-02-20 Maya Chen: Kickoff — scoped mini UX to a single compact card that can be placed on pool pages and the ops quickpanel. Goal: make burst scheduling + cost preview accessible within two clicks.

2026-02-27 Luca Romano: Low-fidelity sketches completed. Two patterns explored: timeline strip with drag-to-slot, and stacked slot list. Chose timeline strip for better temporal context after team critique.

2026-03-03 Maya Chen: Mid-fidelity prototype built. Timeline shows predicted latency bands (p50/p95) derived from historical telemetry linked to model size. Added cost delta badge that updates in real-time as sliders change.

2026-03-04 Diego Alvarez (Eng): Reviewed prototype. Key constraints noted: autoscale granularity limited to 5-minute intervals due to scheduler churn; burst admission must respect pool reservation guarantees. Asked for explicit API contract for 'preview' endpoint to avoid speculative billing.

2026-03-06 Usability test: 6 participants (SREs & platform engineers). Observations: operators loved the rollback CTA and cost preview but found it hard to discover overlapping-slot conflict warnings. Suggested an inline conflict summary and a 'suggested mitigation' CTA.

2026-03-08 Rina Patel (PM): Requested that every cadence change be annotatable (reason + incident tag) for audit logs. Also asked to show SLA risk level when pool capacity dips below configured SLO thresholds.

2026-03-09 Luca Romano: Updated prototype with conflict overlay and annotation modal. Introduced small toast explaining that preview uses a simulated billing estimate pegged to current quantization profile.

2026-03-10 Maya Chen: Preparing handoff. Created interaction spec doc and a trimmed token set for console CSS variables. Noted remaining open question: whether burst slots should be first-class objects in RBAC or only available to pool admins. Tagged ENG-12884 for API work.

2026-03-10 Diego Alvarez (Eng): Quick review comment: recommend limiting max concurrent manual bursts per pool to avoid KV cache thrash; proposed ENG task to simulate cache invalidation rate under bursts. Marked as dependency.
2026-03-10 Rina Patel (PM): In Review — parking this in Design Review for signoff. If approved, schedule dev spike in Cycle 2026-W11 for integration with Dedicated autoscaler service.
engineering_feedback: Autoscale granularity: 5m min step to avoid thrash (scheduler constraint).
Preview endpoint must be read-only and non-billable — return simulated cost and latency bands based on recent 7d telemetry.
Burst admission must check reserved headroom and fallback to model-variant routing if insufficient capacity.
Limit concurrent manual bursts to N per pool (eng to propose N).
Add server-side validation to prevent overlapping bursts that violate SLA tiers.
usability_findings: Operators completed scheduling flow in 1.8 minutes on average with timeline strip vs 2.6m for stacked list.
Rollback CTA reduced anxiety — 5/6 participants noted they'd use it during on-call incidents.
Conflict warnings were missed in first pass; inline summary improved detection to 100% in follow-up testing.
Cost preview is highly valued but must surface confidence band (low/medium/high) to avoid false precision.
next_steps: Resolve RBAC question with Security & PM (decision due 2026-03-14).
Finalize API contract with ENG-12884 and add preview endpoint to ENG sprint for 2026-W11.
Hand off final tokens and interaction specs to eng; include story points for engineering spike to simulate KV cache impact.
Schedule follow-up usability test focused on multi-pool workflows and SLA-risk disclosure (target 2026-03-24).
notes: Design intention: this mini UX should never replace the full Reserve Console; it's an ops quick-path for high-confidence adjustments.
Avoid overloading the card: keep primary actions (schedule, burst-now, rollback) visible; advanced settings live in expanded drawer.
Tie every manual adjustment to an audit annotation for billing reconciliation and post-incident review.
